skos:Concept.skos:scopeNote: {"id": "ab55bc8c-1d99-4831-b3b2-eeed0d8ed39d", "value": "Metal used primarily for roofing and ornamental purposes, being lighter and stronger than lead."}
{"id": "8b7a8c39-402c-414c-9057-a1a635b89e26", "value": "A rectangular alignment stones "}
{"id": "7ee90458-a3d2-4034-b802-b5c7306308ce", "value": "A structure of uncertain function"}
{"id": "134c6171-936b-4b98-81d9-ab64b063ab75", "value": "A continuous vertical stone structure that encloses or divides an area of land"}
{"id": "74bbbd91-4ef0-4884-abbe-03854692c962", "value": "An enclosure for containing livestock"}
{"id": "744d2390-a626-4cac-82d0-08e3575d8d29", "value": "A heaped pile of earth, gravel, sand, rocks, or debris."}
{"id": "597b04a8-95ad-4c25-967d-74d079e41ec0", "value": "A circular alignment of stones"}
{"id": "b6fa0dbb-4585-4e4a-8ee5-a67da7a6567c", "value": "A mound of rough stones built as a memorial or landmark"}
{"id": "903958b3-3458-4901-b009-67b031947153", "value": "A building with a religious function"}
{"id": "3684e15a-0916-4627-8baf-32a20b27ac75", "value": "A site or location that was inhabited"}
{"id": "2563fa73-4b86-44d3-a3da-44ffdd5d99ea", "value": "a fortified building or strategic position"}
{"id": "88322ed1-c448-46de-88ca-facf95ae7cbb", "value": "A dense collection of archaeological material or artefacts spread on the surface, e.g. pottery, lithics, slag etc."}
{"id": "ddb8615d-8009-4663-a270-676c3e6bab55", "value": "Any large refuse heap, mound, or concentration of cultural debris associated with human occupation"}
{"id": "456045cb-c301-4e12-91a9-329efec40ee1", "value": "a set of pools in which seawater is left to evaporate to make salt"}
{"id": "d99700e9-b12b-4be4-af05-bfcab293fff3", "value": "Animal skin that has been hardened or treated by a tanning process."}
{"id": "f74f3887-4f00-4fff-a4f4-14b628a42d5d", "value": "Transparent, hard substance made by fusing soda-silica which solidifies from a molten state."}
{"id": "d27520e8-96ef-4544-a5e8-3cece86d3ecc", "value": "A small stone-built coffin-like box or ossuary used to hold the bodies of the dead"}
{"id": "d3bf47f5-b1ea-40e8-bae4-345a879af1e6", "value": "A precious metal of lustrous white colour with great malleability and ductility."}
{"id": "a46a516b-a003-4705-8796-0276fd1f2449", "value": "A malleable, ductile, ferromagnetic metal widely used for structural and decorative purposes."}

{"id": "c3010549-b3aa-454e-a725-9c492deec794", "value": "Metal used primarily for roof coverings and window fittings. It is easy to work, can be worked cold, and does not rust, which makes it suitable for holding or repelling water."}

{"id": "c0ba8062-5f87-4878-add9-04eeb31a59c4", "value": "Class of elements and alloys that are characteristically lustrous, ductile, fusible and malleable. These are extracted from ore minerals originally existing in nature and processed before becoming a recogniseable metal."}
{"id": "2da2c35c-cdb9-4901-b043-3dfb44e28cfd", "value": "A metallic substance made by combining two or more elements at least one of which is a metal. Use more specific terms where known."}
{"id": "39ef3a08-3065-45c3-abc1-d99a704927e1", "value": "Measure of certainty"}
{"id": "ad9621a4-b427-439c-9d0f-d5c4b97a9c1e", "value": "a hole dug in the ground to receive a coffin or dead body"}

{"id": "bf9926b1-14bc-4069-bff8-6c1d08059c0d", "value": "A short border of stone that surrounds a grave or plot. A grave curb starts a bit below ground, and extends a few inches above the surface of the ground"}
{"id": "dc43ed98-8da8-4bd8-bd2b-b79eb7039d51", "value": "A repository for the remains of the dead. It is generally any structurally enclosed interment space or burial chamber"}
{"id": "d542d45c-d40d-4bac-9983-b8e502292ec6", "value": "A hard silica rich rock, black or brown coloured, commonly found in nodular form."}

{"id": "7be398c4-5eec-4d4b-84a1-4afd459ceb0a", "value": "A building material used for coating walls and ceilings. Plaster can refer to gypsum plaster (also known as plaster of Paris), lime plaster, or cement plaster."}
{"id": "967dcea5-7e02-4dc8-b2ef-505bc91d00b3", "value": "Hard, durable, dark grey stone, the purest native form of silica, which can either be used decoratively or as a main material. "}
{"id": "7b1df655-7147-480c-ae11-d7d51471e057", "value": "A form of volcanic glass with similar properties to FLINT and often used in the manufacture of sharp-edged tools"}
{"id": "045a3b6f-0bc5-472d-a9ca-56ec99277848", "value": "A ceramic made from clay and fired in a kiln or oven. This term has been used interchangeably with EARTHENWARE and with TERRACOTTA."}
{"id": "2edd4c6d-1533-4ddd-b657-ea86db6153b1", "value": "Rock of definite form and size, usually artificially shaped."}

{"id": "ba7a0798-f159-4b23-b0e3-66da49ea7d65", "value": "Use for objects made from coal, or for stray finds of coal where the association with a wreck site is not proven and thus cannot be stated as either cargo or bunkers"}
{"id": "6120e193-5b91-4e1a-bb2f-e911703267fb", "value": "A fine-grained earth which becomes more plastic when water is added and can be moulded and dried to make bricks, tile, pottery, etc."}
{"id": "f3f3b7c4-eda0-4d31-9f4d-b9d08b88cba5", "value": "A semi-precious, fossilised resin usually used for ornamentation and jewellery"}

{"id": "1890dfe0-caab-40c1-a8c4-ec7f1c6231df", "value": "Alabaster is a name applied to varieties of two distinct minerals: gypsum and calcite. The finer kinds of alabaster are employed as an ornamental stone, especially for internal decoration as its softness allows it to be carved into elaborate forms."}
{"id": "2f4b5514-1e21-4d3d-b140-678f47f1dc43", "value": "Natural inorganic substance possessing a definite chemical composition in a crystalline form"}

{"id": "9872ecfa-2783-43ba-a06b-18ce0e06fee0", "value": "Interpretation of resource information"}
{"id": "3ca62d42-f384-43cd-b753-b5b5c847b71c", "value": "Description types used by SHP"}
{"id": "a65c075a-9b18-4c7e-9815-6cc3c5818f61", "value": "Descriptive information from non-field study of resource"}
{"id": "c8d9da87-b3b7-4c68-92a4-bd289ced9448", "value": "Horn is a hollow, bone-like projection consisting mainly of keratin, found on certain animals (sheep, cows, goats, etc.)"}
{"id": "5f2ee333-c55d-4650-9133-91b8c11bf749", "value": "An alloy which is composed predominantly of tin (c.85-99 percent)."}
{"id": "6969b2b3-a469-48f1-b9e4-e131935931b0", "value": "Derived from FISH Object Materials categories, edited by Julian Jensen van Rensburg for SHP project 2019"}
{"id": "883f26e3-005a-4c25-9fb6-802f32efd099", "value": "Pertaining to or deriving from a living organism"}
{"id": "03c96446-941d-450b-a694-5a506b20d12a", "value": "A thin, flexible material made from the pulp of wood or other fibrous matter which is then pressed and dried to form sheets."}
{"id": "54a5c5e4-ce78-49f0-8c85-026543bc9083", "value": "The black, lightweight and porous residue of partly burnt wood."}
{"id": "d30eeb17-2222-4020-bbb0-622f360da5ec", "value": "A hard, compact, unprocessed, fibrous cellulose substance. The roots, trunks and branches of trees and shrubs consist of this tissue."}
{"id": "064b04a2-1b6a-49d6-af75-c7ea11cc4b17", "value": "Woven or tightly packed fibres often used for clothing, housing or packing materials."}
{"id": "0814ee0c-f8c6-4f74-a611-0afda3d7835e", "value": "A hard material formed by firing clay. For pottery, use POTTERY"}
{"id": "65c779ee-968c-4dfd-a2e6-6e03509c9e53", "value": "A hard, white fine-grained substance forming the main part of the tusks of elephants, walruses, hippos and narwhals."}
{"id": "abb0b889-8103-438f-9219-7a43be291209", "value": "A hard, bone-like material obtained from animal teeth"}
{"id": "e49179b9-1341-426e-acb0-3160b9af9ba6", "value": "Hard, protective covering made largely of calcium salts secreted by soft-bodied invertebrate animals"}
{"id": "2b4a2b65-3f27-4d59-b74b-20935070ac7f", "value": "A writing character of figurative appearance, representing a word or a syllable"}
{"id": "b8b76012-e4fd-4c13-97a0-72e307dad1e4", "value": "Words that are written or cut in something"}
{"id": "c181c153-5c93-4b9d-a608-c2615a87da11", "value": "A place set apart for burial or entombment of the dead"}

{"id": "9e19f5dc-4774-4d37-8cbd-930ae43aba46", "value": "A clay-based ceramic fired at low kiln temperatures (c.800-1200 degrees C). Essentially earthenwares are porous and require glazing for most applications. This term has been used interchangeably with TERRACOTTA and with POTTERY."}

{"id": "de3faa7a-1932-43d0-832b-08ce8fd4618e", "value": "A large natural basin or hollow that has been modified. In some instances rainwater is diverted into these by means of a simple line of stones."}

{"id": "216422b8-3cbd-48eb-9793-54b2d75faec4", "value": "Soft, white, porous sedimentary rock, a form of limestone composed of the mineral calcite"}

{"id": "c9c19f8c-daf2-44f0-8bad-64ceca67a247", "value": "Geologically sandstone consists of particles of quartz naturally cemented together by either silica, calcium or iron. It is this geological composition that accounts for the varying colours and grain sizes found in the many building sandstones."}
{"id": "2d790327-b177-449e-a81f-cf4bc1b02dfe", "value": "A burial within a cave or enclosed space"}

{"id": "3fdcc54e-0243-45d3-8788-c8a217f73d60", "value": "Hard, unglazed, brown, versatile earthenware which can be used as a tile or moulded into statuary."}

{"id": "6c81710a-2f74-4c9b-a70c-696d3c81e5ac", "value": "An alloy where the predominant component metal is copper."}
{"id": "85d8eb51-871b-4dee-9bba-c20024ad8100", "value": "Metal alloy with lead as the principal component"}

{"id": "6a77ea3a-a170-4d1e-a73b-4080ed0325dd", "value": "Threat types from UNESCO (https://whc.unesco.org/en/factors/) - also used for classifying disturbance at sites, where disturbance is taken to be threats which have occurred or are in process which have impacted the resource, compared to threats which are likely to apply in future and are risks to the resource but which have not produced significant impacts (yet)."}
{"id": "ddada83f-a504-46b5-b228-9578c0c3cb40", "value": "A burial within a niche, typically found under boulders"}
{"id": "40a0335d-5cda-4560-b6e6-1a0912c2f3f2", "value": "Natural holes and crevices in the bedrock where rainwater is collected"}
{"id": "55db202c-3c10-4b2e-bb34-2954a060c4cd", "value": "The laying of a body in the ground"}
{"id": "23deafd6-75f1-41b5-931b-f13645d9dbbb", "value": "Any of the pieces of hard tissue consisting largely of calcium phosphate that make up the skeleton of a vertebrate animal"}
{"id": "b9505095-c4b7-4122-9ee4-8cf3f0745ed5", "value": "a type of single-chamber megalithic tomb, usually consisting of two or more vertical megaliths supporting a large flat horizontal capstone"}
{"id": "59892047-aa53-40d6-a7c4-e51249ce4734", "value": "A rock art motif that involved an additive process in its production such as the application of paint"}

{"id": "57378c9d-d8c8-4ff9-b9c5-73fc06526c8b", "value": "A hollow space in bedrock, which may or may not be accessible from the surface, and may contain a variety of solid and liquid bodies, including sediments, speleothems and phreatic systems"}
{"id": "7471732b-d643-4e4b-8c29-43e1cadee1c4", "value": "Sedimentary rock consisting mainly of calcium carbonate. Varying in grain size, colour and hardness, quarried and used throughout the world."}
{"id": "bc38bb85-4206-472f-b274-a1429e2a3f64", "value": "Easily formed metal alloy composed of copper and zinc."}
{"id": "07b92c72-189b-43eb-bf84-fbf39e2de455", "value": "A point at which water flows from an aquifer to the earth's surface"}
{"id": "6eee5406-8a29-4f29-9f0b-70fb770654db", "value": "A strong, durable alloy of iron and carbon."}
